definitions.explanation: A casual, friendly farewell expression used to wrap up a conversation. A playful doubling of では (well then) that signals one is leaving or ending contact.

examples.japanese: ではでは、⟦また→また：00969_mata⟧⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧。
⟦{楽|たの}しかった→楽しい：00817_tanoshii⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。ではでは！
⟦そろそろ→そろそろ：01259_sorosoro⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、ではでは、{気|き}をつけて⟦{帰|かえ}って→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: It's about time, so well then, take care getting home.

notes:
A casual farewell formed by doubling ⟦では→では：02945_deha⟧. The reduplication gives it a lighter, friendlier, slightly playful tone compared to a single ⟦では→では：02945_deha⟧. Commonly used among friends, in online chats, and in informal emails. It signals a gentle, unhurried departure rather than an abrupt goodbye.

The tone is warm and relaxed — not appropriate for formal situations. In text-based communication (LINE, email), it often appears at the very end of a message.

REGISTER:
Casual. Used with friends, family, and close acquaintances. For more formal farewells, use {失礼|しつれい}します or ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦では→では：02945_deha⟧: well then — the base form, slightly more neutral and can be used in semi-formal contexts
- ⟦じゃあ→じゃあ：02989_jaa⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: see you — another casual farewell, very common in spoken Japanese
- ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧: well then — more formal, used in business and polite conversation
- バイバイ: bye-bye — very casual, often used by younger speakers and children
